title: [Chapitre] IV. Analysis situs (première mouture) : notes manuscrites (10/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pages 31-33): Grothendieck is trying to axiomatize a 'structure de contrôle' / 'contexte' for a pointless combinatorial topology ('topologie combinatoire sans points'). This belongs to the Analysis situs / tame topology programme of the Esquisse. On p.31 his study of pseudo-disks (D, ∂D) showed that 'lieux' in D−∂D cannot simply be subsets: they carry extra data, an equivalence or 'order' tied to ∂D. He therefore drops his earlier model, in which a control structure was a set L of loci together with distinguished families of subsets called 'figures'.

On this page he replaces it by an abstract quadruple C = (M, ≪, R_M, 𝓕):
- M is a set of 'multiplicités' (objects; on p.33 called multiplicities).
- ≪ is the refinement relation, marked 'raffinement' and 'rel. d'ordre'.
- R_M is a reflexive symmetric relation, marked 'compatibilité' and 'rel. sym. réfl.'.
- 𝓕 is a family of subsets of M, the figures.

The diagonal margin notes two points:
- R_M is redundant: x R_M y iff there is a figure F in 𝓕 with x, y ∈ F.
- Conversely, he wonders whether ≪ and R_M determine 𝓕, with a 'NB vérifier'.

His stated plan is first to isolate a good system of axioms and a geometric terminology, noting along the way which axioms he will be led to impose.

Sub-context: given by a subset M' ⊂ M stable under refinement (if X ∈ M', every refinement of X lies in M'). It carries the relations induced by ≪ and R_M, and presumably the induced figures. He warns explicitly that it is not automatic that the axioms to be imposed on a context are stable under passage to a sub-context.

Page 33 then gives the axioms:
- Cont 1: define X ≤ Y iff X ≪ Y and X is compatible with Y; then ≤ is a partial order.
- Fig 2: a figure is pairwise compatible and is a 'partie finissante' (a down-closed subset) of (M, ≤).
- Fig 3: down-closed subsets of figures are figures; the empty set is a figure.
- Fig 1: each principal down-set M_{≤X} is a figure (the 'figure élémentaire' of X).
- Corollary: if Y, Z ≤ X then Y and Z are compatible.

In modern terms: a poset with a reflexive symmetric compatibility relation, and a family of pairwise-consistent down-closed subsets, containing the principal ideals and closed under down-closed subsets. Figures thus behave like simplices of an abstract simplicial complex built on a poset, or like configurations of a domain-theoretic structure.
errors: The margin suggestion that (≪, R_M) determine 𝓕 is false in general. The axioms only force each figure to be a pairwise-compatible down-set. Recovering 𝓕 from R_M requires an extra 'flag/clique' axiom: every pairwise-compatible down-closed (possibly finite) set is a figure. Compare a simplicial complex versus its flag complex (the boundary of a triangle is not a clique complex). Grothendieck himself flags this with 'NB vérifier'.

The characterization of R_M as co-membership in a figure is consistent with the page 33 axioms. Compatible pairs lie in a common figure via M_{≤X} only when one element is ≤ the other; for incomparable pairs, R_M must be taken as the definition or imposed as an axiom.

His warning about sub-contexts is correct. Closure of M' under refinement gives down-closure, but an axiom such as 'compatible ⇒ lies in a common figure', or any existence axiom, need not pass to M'. No error, just an acknowledged gap.

ideas.what: Point-free combinatorial 'context': a set of objects with a refinement relation, a reflexive symmetric compatibility relation, and a family of 'figures' (subsets)
ideas.modern_name: Poset with consistency relation; close to event structures / coherence spaces / mereotopology
ideas.usually_credited_to: Nielsen–Plotkin–Winskel (event structures, 1981); Girard (coherence spaces, 1986-87); Whitehead / Clarke (point-free mereotopology)
ideas.where_published: Tame topology programme only sketched in Esquisse d'un programme (1984); no axiomatics of this kind published

ideas.what: Abandoning 'loci = subsets' because loci in a pseudo-disk carry extra order/equivalence data relative to the boundary
ideas.modern_name: Point-free / locale-like topology where opens are not sets of points
ideas.where_published: Spirit of SGA4 topos theory (sites without points); not in this combinatorial form

ideas.what: Sub-context as a refinement-closed subset with induced relations, with a caveat that the axioms need not be hereditary
ideas.modern_name: Induced substructure on a down-closed subset (restriction of an event structure / sub-poset)

missed.claim: Grothendieck's 'contexte' (page 33 axioms) is essentially the notion of a prime event structure with configurations, or of a coherence space / Scott information system. Elements are partially ordered by ≤; R_M is the complement of conflict; figures are down-closed, pairwise-consistent sets containing the principal ideals [X] and closed under down-closed subsets. The corollary 'Y, Z ≤ X ⇒ Y compatible with Z' is the conflict-heredity axiom. Grothendieck arrived at this independently in 1986 as a foundation for point-free combinatorial topology. The link between event-structure/domain semantics and tame/combinatorial topology of pseudo-disks is not made in the literature.
missed.quote: C = (M, ≪, R_M, 𝓕 famille de parties de M) ... compatibilité ... rel. d'ordre ... raffinement ... rel. sym. réfl.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Event structures and configuration spaces are now studied topologically (directed topology, concurrency via cubical complexes, Winskel's 'configuration complexes'). Grothendieck's motivation runs the other way, using such structures to encode point-free topology of surfaces. This is a modest but genuine cross-field parallel.

missed.claim: The programme of a 'topologie combinatoire sans points' axiomatized by contexts (M, ≪, R_M, 𝓕), aimed at pseudo-disks and tame topology, is announced here and was never developed in public.
missed.quote: n'est pas valable pour la 'topologie combinatoire sans points'. Donc il faudra prendre la donnée de C = (M, ≪, R_M, 𝓕)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is one of the few concrete attempts by Grothendieck to give an axiomatics for 'topologie modérée' as announced in the Esquisse. It is of historical interest and a possible starting point for o-minimal / tame combinatorial foundations.

deep.surprise_reason: This is an intermediate set-up page, but it documents Grothendieck's own point-free combinatorial axiomatics for tame topology. The structure he lands on independently mirrors event structures / coherence spaces from computer science. That is an unpublished and curious parallel, though the page itself contains no theorem.
transcription_corrections: Margin: read 'R_M résultera de ≪, 𝓕 car si x, y ∈ M, x R_M y ssi ∃ F ∈ 𝓕 tel que x, y ∈ F'. The stray 'x, y ∈ 𝓕' in the machine text should be dropped.
'à l'intention de nous [?] de voir plus tard' is probably just '... à imposer, quitte à voir plus tard' or similar; 'nous' is doubtful.
'Sous-contexte : est défini par une partie M' qui est stable dans M par ≪': 'arbitraire' is doubtful. The phrase continues 'i.e. si X est dans M', tout raffinement de X y est aussi.'
The annotations under the tuple read roughly 'compatibilité' (above, attached to R_M), 'raffinement / rel. d'ordre' (attached to ≪) and 'rel. sym. réfl.' (attached to R_M).
